utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can proceed with calling the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number, IT-99-36-T, the Prosecutor versus Radoslav Brdjanin and Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Brdjanin. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRDJANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I can hear you and understand you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. General Talic, good afternoon to you. Can you hear me in a language that you can understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED TALIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I can hear you in a language I can understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Anna Richterova, and Julian Nicholls for the Prosecution, assisted by Denise Gustin, case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, madam. Good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Radoslav Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRBOJEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. I am attorney Milan Trbojevic with lead counsel Mr. Ackerman and our assistant Marela Jevtovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, and good afternoon to you three. Appearances for General Momir Talic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic and Ms. Natasha Ivanovic-Fauveau for General Talic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And good afternoon to you both. I thank you. Before we proceed and before we go into closed session, we have given our proposed schedule for breaks a second thought, taking into consideration the plight of Mr. Ackerman as well as the not so obvious but definitely concurring plight of Mr. Nicholls. Instead of breaking as we had proposed to you yesterday, we will be breaking on the 13th of November, resuming on the 25th, which basically means the following, so that there are no surprises: The 13th is subject to changes. If I find -- and usually when the winter flight schedule to Malta comes into operation, there are no flights on Wednesday and on Thursday, which would mean that I would have to fly on Tuesday evening. But if there is a flight on Wednesday, then we will work on the 13th. This is -- this is the idea. Okay? So until now and until further notice, we will not be working on the 13th, 14th, 15th. Then you have 16th and 17th, which is a Saturday and a Sunday respectively. And then we will not be working on the 18th, 19th, 20th, and 21st just to fit in Thanksgiving. The 22nd is court maintenance, in any case. And then 23rd, apart from being Judge Orie's birthday is a Saturday. And then you have Sunday. And we will resume on the 25th. And if you happen to arrive on Sunday, the 24th, Mr. Ackerman, there is Scheveningen Sunday concert at 12.15 -- at 11.00 till 12.15, and on that day it's Judge El Madhi's birthday. So one after the other. We will resume on the 25th. The only change that there might be is the 13th. If there is a flight -- if I can fly on Wednesday, rather than Tuesday, then we will have a sitting on the 13th. Okay? So that will give you a break of 12 days -- 12 running days.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I just want to say I'm very grateful to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're welcome, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And probably even more grateful is my wife.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no comment on this change. I just wanted to let the Court know that I've spoken with Ms. Korner and she would prefer that one way or we try to work some more days before the end of the year. She's heard about the breaks. I think it was 61 working days under the current scheme. And I just wanted the Court to know we would prefer to try to fit some more days in if we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're going to work tomorrow, in any case, which is your national day. Okay. And if you want to turn up on the 21st of November, you're welcome. No. I'll -- we'll take note of that. But on the other hand, I -- as I tried to explain to you two days ago or whenever it was, it's no use trying to extract blood from rocks or try to make a horse drink once you've taken the horse to the river or to the spring. I mean, we all need to work at a pace which we can take. And please do understand that we are understaffed. I'm taking this up myself with the rest of the Judges with the administration, because I can't allow a situation whereby I have two or three persons that have a workload which makes me wonder sometimes how they can carry. And the same applies to you. I mean, to you and to us and to everyone. So let's pull the curtains down, go into closed session. And in the meantime -- oh, the usher has to bring down the curtains before she can actually bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: The second piece of information is that because we are so delayed, we unfortunately will have to make another change in the order of witnesses. I have already consulted this with the team of -- Defence teams, and they do not oppose -- they do not object. And it is that next witness will go as scheduled, 7.193. But the further witness will be 7.13, and then will be 7.62.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. And in fact you had already -- or either you or Ms. Korner had already advised us that 7.13, who was the first one on the list, would be coming forward to give evidence in the first week of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes. It is true, but he was scheduled after 7 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That's no problem. And now the other thing that comes to my mind -- and it may be that I am -- that you are going to consider what I am going to say as superfluous -- but in case for the 15th we will be dealing with a new witness, make sure that the shifting to the morning session does coincide with his coming over. I don't know how you work it out, but make sure that we don't sit in the morning while we expect the witness to arrive from wherever in the afternoon, like Mr. Ackerman and Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My only question, Your Honour, is -- I think I agree with you to bring the witness in and talk to him, but I wonder if there's really a point in starting -- actually starting the direct examination and talking for ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, no. I said bring the witness in. And at least you can -- I can have a word with him and you can also start with the very preliminaries. You know, I mean, it's -- those you can get rid of today, you know, anyway.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This witness does not enjoy any protective measures, if I remember well. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You may sit down. You may sit down. And good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's only because I have been a Judge for a long number of years and unfortunately this is not the first time that I had to deal with a circumstance like this that I can address you with relative ease. But I do feel embarrassed, and I feel embarrassed because I know that you have been waiting to come into this courtroom and start your evidence for over two hours. Under normal circumstances, I would have told you that shouldn't happen, but it had to happen because the previous witness took longer to finish his testimony; and therefore, we couldn't start with yours before we concluded his. I am sure you understand, but please do accept our apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you for understanding. Now please stand up. The lady standing next to you is going to give you a piece of paper, on which there is a text -- the text of a solemn declaration to tell us the truth in the course of your testimony. It's the equivalent of an oath, and you are a summons server, familiar with court proceedings, I would imagine, I would suppose, and you would know what I am talking about. What I would like to ask you to do now is to proceed with reading that solemn declaration aloud, with the understanding that that's going to be your undertaking to tell us the truth and the whole truth in the course of your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may sit down. Now, today you are going to be asked very few questions, because we have got very little time left. And then the Prosecution will really start examining you in chief tomorrow when we resume with our -- with the hearings at 2.15 in the afternoon. Now, let me explain to you what's going to happen. First of all, you are in a courtroom, as you are well aware. We are the three Judges presiding over this case. I am the Presiding Judge. My name is Agius and I come from Malta. To my right, I have Judge Janu from the Czech Republic. To my left, I have Judge Taya from Japan. We will be the ones who will ultimately decide this case. You will be examined in chief by the Prosecution, and the person responsible for your examination will be Mr. Nicholls, who is the person who I understand you already know. At the end of the direct examination, there will be what we call cross-examination, and there will be two cross-examinations, one by each of the two Defence teams. The first Defence team is the -- is that which you see to your left. In the front row is the Defence team for Radoslav Brdjanin, one of the accused. In the back row, there are the Defence counsel for General Momir Talic. They will be cross-examining you after that -- the examination-in-chief has come to an end. Mr. Nicholls, you can start with perhaps a few --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'll try to get just get out his personal background, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And I also apologise that you had to wait. Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: My name is Bekir Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were born in January 1959 in Cazin municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your ethnic origin is Bosniak?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what your faith is, what religious beliefs you practice.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: I'm a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And when you were a very young child you moved to Sanski Most municipality; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you grew up there and spent really all of your life there, up and through until almost the end of 1992.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: You were married in 1992, living in Sanski Most, and you had a child.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: No. I was married in 1988, in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That -- my question wasn't clear. That's right. And in Sanski Most you started -- you worked mainly for the Sanski Most municipal court as a summons server; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And you were also a driver and would drive the judges and other officials of the court to different places in Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, a kind of a court commissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And in 1991 and 1992 were you a member of any political party?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Prior to 1991 I think you'd agree that relations between the three ethnicities in Sanski Most were good, were normal.

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: In late 1991 these relationships were -- in late 1991 into the beginning of 1992, did those relations change?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And they essentially broke down; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEKIR DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't know if we should break, Your Honour, or beginning -- substantive direct. I only have a couple --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. If you feel more comfortable that way, we will do so. So as I promised you, it will be a short session today. We will see you again tomorrow at 2.15. How long do you expect your direct to last, Mr. Nicholls, if I may ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: As I said, I've been wrong. I'm going to try to be very quick and finish in about two hours. And hopefully he can finish tomorrow totally. That's what is my goal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I don't dare ask the Defence, not having heard the witness give evidence. So we'll see what happens tomorrow. Anyway, I think the witness can be escorted out. Ms. -- Madam Registrar, you can advise Judge Mumba we will be shifting 15th to 18th. And then if there is a problem on the 15th, well, we'll -- we'll see what we can do at that point in time. Okay? But in the meantime, one can calculate if we start with this witness tomorrow - tomorrow is Thursday - Friday -- would 7 -- do you reckon that you will finish 7.13 and 7.62 during next week?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to finish 7.13 on Friday. So it's my wish and my goal to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We seem to be -- to be living on wishes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If not wishful thinking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It would be great if we could conclude, because you know that next week there's only sittings from Monday to Wednesday. Then Thursday and Friday we have the plenary next week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact it's -- I'm being reminded, actually. I should have remembered. But basically we have a sitting on the 8th and on the 9th. The 10th afternoon is being reserved for the pre-hearing, or call it whatever you like, on the contempt issue. So look -- look into that, Madam Richterova, a little bit and see what the situation seems to be in anticipation of the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: We know the situation -- or more or less we can state that we will have one witness who will go for a long time after we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's BT21. No?

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RICHTEROVA
utterances.text: So after we finish 7.62 - which I expect can start and be finished on Monday - we can start BT21.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anyway, we'll play it by the ear and then we'll see. Yes. We'll see how -- what position we are this Friday first before we talk of next week and the week after. Okay? Thanks. So good evening, or enjoy what's left of it and this beautiful weather, and we will reconvene tomorrow at 2.15. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: at 6.31 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday, the 4th day of July, 2002, at 2.15 p.m. 24
